label: Sequence-start unit: first token in {h,k,l,o,v,x,3} (and the step after), plus early copy steps
explanation: Fires almost only near the two ends of the sequence boundary: the first two original steps (t=0,1; about 52% of mass) and the first copy steps (recall_idx 1-4, about 45% of mass). It is essentially silent at the <DEL> step and at original positions t>=3. At t=0 the activation depends only on the token: it fires every time the first token is h, k, l, o, v, x or 3, and never for any other token. At t=1 it fires mostly when the previous (first) token was in that set. In the copy phase, the input there is orig(0), orig(1) and so on, and firing depends on the token and also on context, which this predicate does not capture. It is most frequent for 1, s, q, 2, 0, u, n at recall_idx 1, but even those reach only 20-30% precision. The largest activations (around 0.5-0.6) come at the first copy steps, e.g. 2 then b, or s, in sequences whose first token is not in the t=0 set. Position alone (t<=1 or recall_idx 1-4) covers about 95% of mass but with only 10% precision, so token identity and hidden-state context strongly gate it.
